A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OBLIVIATE and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The complete versions support reliable comparison, including matching WMDP results moved from the main text into the appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original unlearning experiments on Harry Potter, WMDP, and TOFU, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds adversarial-baseline comparisons, relearning and quantization results, and jailbreak examples.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains GPT-4o token identification, BM25 document selection, the three retain-document categories, LoRA, and the same masked, distillation, and world-fact losses. The added attacks evaluate the method rather than modify it.

E1.justification: Harry Potter, WMDP, and all three TOFU subsets remain unchanged. V2 adds adversarially suffixed harmful-generation prompts in Table 9, extending input-scenario coverage without adding a benchmark corpus.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds evaluated Adv_GA and Adv_NPO baselines for Zephyr-7B; Adv_GA also appears in the new attack comparison. ELM was already evaluated in v1 despite its omission from that version's WMDP baseline prose. Relocated Llama3 comparisons remain present.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial additional evaluation procedures: relearning using 10% of the forget set, 4-bit quantization, and jailbreak prompting. Figure 3 also evaluates trade-offs using mean WMDP score reduction against averaged MMLU accuracy and fluency. Existing benchmark partitions and unlearning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds relearning and quantization robustness comparisons in Table 6, jailbreak cases in Table 9, and a WMDP Pareto trade-off analysis in Figure 3. Table 17 expands the contextual case study with responses before unlearning. Existing loss ablations, TOFU-size analysis, and hyperparameter comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging fluency scores across five GPT-4o conversations and retain the same mean/variance reporting. V2 introduces no additional seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V2 adds adversarial-baseline scores, attack outcomes, jailbreak responses, and outputs before unlearning. Table 6 newly reports OBLIVIATE Bio/Cyber scores of 49.2/31.2 after relearning and 29.5/24.7 after int4 quantization; these concern new conditions. Retained benchmark values match. Section 4.3 also corrects Llama3 fluency variance from 0.90 to 2.01, matching the table in both versions.

T1.justification: The formal unlearning setup, loss equations, DRMA definition, and appendix Transformer/LoRA mathematics are unchanged. The expanded discussion of generation and leakage adds interpretation rather than a mathematical derivation or guarantee.

C1.justification: The central method, forgetting, utility, and fluency claims remain. Introduction contribution IV and the conclusion explicitly broaden the claimed evaluation contribution to include robustness testing against relearning, quantization, and jailbreaking.

C2.justification: V2 adds a delayed-leakage explanation and stronger no-leakage interpretation for DRMA, interprets the new Pareto and attack results, and identifies other attacks as outside scope. Section 6 adds computational cost and dependence on commercial annotation models as limitations. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: The stated code-access location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. V2 also newly specifies sampling-based decoding for Figure 2. Existing hardware, optimizer settings, loss weights, prompt templates, and BM25 instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on relearning, adversarial unlearning, jailbreaking, and unlearning reversibility, including Lo et al., Yuan et al., Zou et al., and Xu et al. Appendix A gains a threat-focused discussion, while the established method positioning and unlearning taxonomy remain.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized revisions to the introduction, DRMA explanation, results, conclusion, and author information, plus acknowledgments. Appendix headings are rearranged imperfectly: 'Prompt setting' precedes the memorization discussion, while the actual prompt instructions appear under Appendix D.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn and enlarged, Figure 3 and two evidence tables are added, and the contextual example table gains a before-unlearning column. WMDP model panels are redistributed and consolidated in appendix Table 18. These substantially revise the visual presentation beyond numerical additions.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the robustness evidence through quantitative attack comparisons and adversarial baselines, while clearer diagrams and before-unlearning examples improve interpretation. The gain is limited: Table 6 still shows substantial recovery under relearning, Table 9 provides only five illustrative jailbreak cases, and the stronger DRMA no-leakage language lacks a new guarantee. The misplaced prompt appendix heading also introduces a small organizational defect.
